This study aimed to investigate the dose-dependent effects of vitamin D supplementation on depressive and anxiety symptoms in adults. We systematically searched PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science up to December 2022 to identify randomized controlled trials evaluating the effects of vitamin D

studies.title: The impact of vitamin D supplementation on depression and anxiety in young individuals with depression and vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency.
studies.abstract: This study evaluates the effects of vitamin D supplementation on depression and anxiety in young people with major depression and vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency. This partially randomized patient preference trial enrolled outpatients aged 10-24 with major depression and vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency. Participants who expressed a preference received vitamin D, while others were randomly assigned to vitamin D or placebo groups. Randomization was performed using computer-generated random numbers in blocks of four, with allocation concealed from researchers, participants, and treating physicians. Supplementation groups received 4,800 IU of vitamin D3 daily for 8 weeks. The primary outcome was assessor-rated depressive symptoms measured using the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. Secondary outcomes were self-reported depression (Beck Depression Inventory-II) and anxiety (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7). A total of 108 participants were included and assigned to three groups: randomized vitamin D (RVD, n = 41; mild/moderate-to-severe depression, 23/18), preference vitamin D (PVD, n = 28; 16/12), and placebo (PL, n = 39; 23/16). Among adolescents (10-19 years), 9/8 in the RVD group had mild/moderate-to-severe depression, compared to 9/8 in the PVD group, and 10/7 in the PL group. There was no significant difference in depression between the RVD and PL groups (B =  - 0.30, 95% CI [- 1.81, 1.21], p = 0.698), however anxiety was reduced in the RVD group (B =  - 1.78, 95% CI [- 3.35, - 0.32], p = 0.026). Subgroup analyses revealed that the participants with moderate-to-severe depression in the RVD groups had reduced depression and anxiety versus placebo. However, the subgroup of adolescents with moderate-to-severe depression did not differ in all outcome scores in the RVD versus placebo. There were no significant differences between the PVD and RVD groups. No differences in hypercalcemia or hyperphosphatemia were observed. The trial was completed. Vitamin D supplementation may benefit young people with moderate-to-severe depression and vitamin D insufficiency/deficiency. While sample size constraints favor an exploratory interpretation of these findings, this study provides a valuable piece of the puzzle; future trials are essential to complete the clinical picture.

studies.title: Effect of vitamin D supplementation on fatigue and mood among perimenopausal women.
studies.abstract: Perimenopausal women often experience fatigue and mood disturbances, which may be associated with vitamin D deficiency. Therefore, it is of interest to investigate the effect of vitamin D supplementation on fatigue and mood in perimenopausal women with vitamin D deficiency. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial included 100 women who received either vitamin D3 or a placebo for 6 months. Results showed significant improvements in both fatigue and mood in the vitamin D group compared to placebo. Multivariate analysis confirmed vitamin D supplementation as a predictor of these improvements. Thus, vitamin D supplementation can effectively alleviate fatigue and improve mood in perimenopausal women with vitamin D deficiency.

studies.title: The effect of hormonal contraceptives combined with vitamin D3 supplements on sexual dysfunction in women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized double-bl
studies.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by reproductive and endocrine abnormalities. The present study aimed to assess the effect of oral contraceptive pills (OCPs) and vitamin D3 on sexual dysfunction in women with PCOS and vitamin D3 deficiency. This randomized double-blind placebo-controlled clinical trial was conducted in Iran between January and April 2019. The Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) questionnaires were filled out for all participants and their serum levels of vitamin D3 were measured. Women with PCOS and vitamin D3 deficiency were divided into 2 equal groups (A and B) with a table of random numbers (n = 35/ each). Both groups were given vitamin D3 (50,000 IU/w) for 12 week. The case group was given low-dose OCP for 3 months and a similar placebo was given to the control group. Vitamin D3 level and sexual function were assessed in both groups at 3 and 6 months after taking OCP. There was no statistically significant difference between the two groups in demographic characteristic such as weight (69.54 ± 10.34 vs 70.17 ± 10.60, P = 0.803). Both groups treated with vitamin D3 exhibited increased sexual function scores at the beginning of the study (P = 0.03) and 3 months (P = 0.01) after taking OCP. Examination of sexual function variables showed that sexual desire in the control group was greater than in the OCP-treated group at 3 (P = 0.009) and 6 (P = 0.01) months after entering the study. The results of the study showed that the score of women's sexual performance increased in all areas, especially in the area of sexual desire, with the use of vitamin D3. The simultaneous use of OCP with vitamin D3 to improve sexual performance in these women had no significant difference with the use of vitamin D3 alone. According to the research findings, it is recommended that vitamin D3 supplementation can be used to increase the quality of life and improve sexual function in PCOS women.

studies.title: Does Vitamin D3 Supplementation Improve Depression Scores among Rural Adolescents? A Randomized Controlled Trial.
studies.abstract: Contemporary evidence has been established demonstrating that stunted vitamin D levels are associated with depression, poor mood, and other mental disorders. Individuals with normal vitamin D levels have a much lower probability of developing depression. Improving vitamin D levels by supplementation has shown betterment in depressive patients among different age groups. The objective of this study was to assess the effect of vitamin D supplementation on depression scores among rural adolescents. This study was a cluster randomized controlled trial carried out for a period of 3 years among adolescents from rural Kolar. The sample size was calculated based on previous research and was determined to be 150 for each group. The intervention arm received 2250 IU of vitamin D, and the control arm received a lower dose of 250 IU of vitamin D for 9 weeks. To assess sociodemographic status, a pretested, semi-structured questionnaire was used, and, to assess depression, the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II) was used. A baseline assessment was carried out for vitamin D status and depression status, followed by a post-intervention assessment. From the start of the trial, the participants were contacted every week by the pediatric team to investigate any side effects. Out of 235 school students in the vitamin D supplementation arm, 129 (54.9%) belonged to the 15 years age group, 124 (52.8%) were boys, and 187 (79.6%) belonged to a nuclear family. Out of 216 school students in the calcium supplementation arm, 143 (66.2%) belonged to the 15 years age group, 116 (53.7%) were girls, and 136 (63%) belonged to a nuclear family. By comparing Beck depression scores before and after the intervention, it was found that the vitamin D intervention arm showed a statistically significant reduction in Beck depression scores. The present study showed that vitamin D supplementation reduced depression scores, showing some evidence that nutritional interventions for mental health issues such as depression are an excellent option. Vitamin D supplementation in schools can have numerous beneficiary effects on health while mutually benefiting mental health.

studies.title: Effect of Long-term Vitamin D3 Supplementation vs Placebo on Risk of Depression or Clinically Relevant Depressive Symptoms and on Change in Mood Scores: A Rando
studies.abstract: Low levels of 25-hydroxyvitamin D have been associated with higher risk for depression later in life, but there have been few long-term, high-dose large-scale trials. To test the effects of vitamin D3 supplementation on late-life depression risk and mood scores. There were 18 353 men and women aged 50 years or older in the VITAL-DEP (Vitamin D and Omega-3 Trial-Depression Endpoint Prevention) ancillary study to VITAL, a randomized clinical trial of cardiovascular disease and cancer prevention among 25 871 adults in the US. There were 16 657 at risk for incident depression (ie, no depression history) and 1696 at risk for recurrent depression (ie, depression history but no treatment for depression within the past 2 years). Randomization occurred from November 2011 through March 2014; randomized treatment ended on December 31, 2017, and this was the final date of follow-up. Randomized assignment in a 2 × 2 factorial design to vitamin D3 (2000 IU/d of cholecalciferol) and fish oil or placebo; 9181 were randomized to vitamin D3 and 9172 were randomized to matching placebo. The primary outcomes were the risk of depression or clinically relevant depressive symptoms (total of incident and recurrent cases) and the mean difference in mood scores (8-item Patient Health Questionnaire depression scale [PHQ-8]; score range, 0 points [least symptoms] to 24 points [most symptoms]; the minimal clinically important difference for change in scores was 0.5 points). Among the 18 353 randomized participants (mean age, 67.5 [SD, 7.1] years; 49.2% women), the median treatment duration was 5.3 years and 90.5% completed the trial (93.5% among those alive at the end of the trial). Risk of depression or clinically relevant depressive symptoms was not significantly different between the vitamin D3 group (609 depression or clinically relevant depressive symptom events; 12.9/1000 person-years) and the placebo group (625 depression or clinically relevant depressive symptom events; 13.3/1000 person-years) (hazard ratio, 0.97 [95% CI, 0.87 to 1.09]; P = .62); there were no significant differences between groups in depression incidence or recurrence. No significant differences were observed between treatment groups for change in mood scores over time; mean change in PHQ-8 score was not significantly different from zero (mean difference for change in mood scores, 0.01 points [95% CI, -0.04 to 0.05 points]). Among adults aged 50 years or older without clinically relevant depressive symptoms at baseline, treatment with vitamin D3 compared with placebo did not result in a statistically significant difference in the incidence and recurrence of depression or clinically relevant depressive symptoms or for change in mood scores over a median follow-up of 5.3 years. These findings do not support the use of vitamin D3 in adults to prevent depression. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT01169259 and NCT01696435.

studies.title: Vitamin D3 supplementation and treatment outcomes in patients with depression (D3-vit-dep).
studies.abstract: To examine whether vitamin D supplementation in patients with depression would result in a reduction in Hamilton D-17 depression score (primary outcome) at 3 and 6 months compared to controls and to explore the correlations between serum vitamin D and symptoms of depression, wellbeing, systolic blood pressure, and waist circumference. In this outpatient multicentre study conducted between 2010 and 2013, patients, 18-65 years old, diagnosed with mild to severe depression were randomly assigned to receive D supplementation 70 micrograms daily or placebo on top of standard treatment. Participants, care givers and those assessing the outcomes were blinded to group assignment. At baseline, 23 patients had a normal 25(OH)D level, 22 had insufficiency (< 25 nmol/L), and 17 had deficiency (25-50 nmol/L). No significant reduction in depression was seen after vitamin D supplementation compared to placebo at Hamilton (18.4-18.0; p = 0.73 at 12 weeks). Vitamin D supplementation did not provide a reduction in symptom score among patients with depression. Trial registration The trial was registered in the National Board of Health (EudraCT: 2011-002585-20) and in ClinicalTrials.Gov (NCT01390662).

studies.title: A randomized controlled trial of vitamin D supplementation on perinatal depression: in Iranian pregnant mothers.
studies.abstract: Mood disorders in pregnancy and post-partum period are common and considered as a public health issue. Researchers have studied the relationship between low serum vitamin D concentration and perinatal depression, although no clinical trial has been conducted on vitamin D's effects on depression related to childbirth. This study evaluated the effect of vitamin D3 supplementation on perinatal depression scores. This randomized clinical trial was done in pregnant women who were under prenatal care in a teaching hospital in Shiraz, Iran. The inclusion criteria were: being 18 years or older, no history of mental illness and internal diseases, a singleton live fetus, without any pregnancy complications, gestational age of 26-28 weeks upon enrollment, and depression score of 0 to 13. The Edinburgh Postnatal Depression scale was used to evaluate depression scores. A total of 169 participants were assigned to the two groups of placebo and vitamin D through block randomization design. Vitamin D group received 2000 IU vitamin D3 daily from 26 to 28 weeks of gestation until childbirth. Maternal serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations were measured at baseline and childbirth. Besides, depression scores were evaluated four times: at 26-28 and 38-40 weeks of gestation, and finally at 4 and 8 weeks after birth. The two groups were similar in relation to baseline 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations. However, at childbirth, the vitamin D group had significantly higher 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentration in comparison to the control group (p < 0.001). At baseline, no correlation was observed between 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentration and depression score (r = 0.13, p = 0.09). There was no significant difference between the two study groups in relation to the baseline depression score. While, the vitamin D group had greater reduction in depression scores than the control group at 38-40 weeks of gestation (p = 0.01) also, at 4 and 8 weeks after birth (p < 0.001). The present trial showed that consuming 2000 IU vitamin D3 daily during late pregnancy was effective in decreasing perinatal depression levels. We suggest further clinical trial in pregnant mothers who are at risk for postnatal depression. Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials  IRCT2015020310327N11 . Date of registration: March 9th 2015.

studies.title: Molecular Crosstalk of Vitamin D3 with cGAS-STING and BDNF Pathways in a Rat Model of Chronic Stress.
studies.abstract: Neuroinflammation via the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) pathway and reduced hippocampal brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) expression are key mechanisms underlying stress-induced depression. Vitamin D3, acting through the vitamin D receptor (VDR), is known to possess immunomodulatory and neurotrophic properties, but its role under chronic stress remains unclear. This study investigated the effects of vitamin D3 on chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS)-induced neuroinflammation and neurotrophic deficits in male Wistar rats. Thirty-two rats were divided into four groups: control, CUMS only, CUMS + vitamin D3 (1000 IU/kg), and CUMS + vitamin D3 (10,000 IU/kg). Vitamin D3 was injected intramuscularly three times weekly for 28 days. Hippocampal mRNA expression of cGAS-STING pathway markers, BDNF, microglial activation marker Iba1, and pro-inflammatory cytokines was quantified by RT-qPCR, and relative expression was calculated using the 2-ΔΔCt method. Serum vitamin D3 and corticosterone concentrations were measured by ELISA. CUMS significantly reduced serum vitamin D3, increased corticosterone, activated hippocampal cGAS-STING signaling, upregulated inflammatory mediators and Iba1, and suppressed VDR and BDNF mRNA expression (all p < 0.05). Vitamin D3 administration effectively restored serum vitamin D3, normalized corticosterone levels, attenuated cGAS-STING activation and inflammatory gene expression, reduced microglial activation, and enhanced hippocampal VDR and BDNF mRNA expression (all p < 0.05). These findings demonstrate that vitamin D3 alleviates CUMS-induced hippocampal inflammation and neurotrophic deficits through coordinated modulation of immune signaling and BDNF, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic approach for stress-related brain disorders.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A fat-soluble vitamin your skin makes from sunlight; also taken as a supplement.
explanation.what_it_is: Vitamin D3, also called cholecalciferol, is a steroid-like compound your body produces when skin is exposed to sunlight, or absorbs from food and supplements. It's a fat-soluble vitamin, meaning it dissolves in fat rather than water, so it accumulates in fatty tissues and the liver. Most supplements deliver it as a crystalline powder in capsules or liquid form, and it's one of the most commonly used micronutrient supplements worldwide.
explanation.how_it_works_line: Converts into a hormone that regulates calcium, bone strength, immune function, and blood sugar.
explanation.how_it_works: After you ingest or produce vitamin D3, your body converts it first in the liver, then in the kidneys, into an active hormone called calcitriol. This hormone acts like a master regulator: it binds to vitamin D receptors (docking sites on cells throughout the body) that control how much calcium you absorb in the gut, how bone is built and broken down, how immune cells behave, and how your pancreas releases insulin to manage blood sugar. Because vitamin D receptors are found in hundreds of cell types — bone, immune cells, pancreatic beta cells, and brain regions involved in mood — vitamin D influences multiple systems at once. Without adequate vitamin D, your body struggles to absorb calcium, maintain bone density, regulate immune responses, and stabilize blood sugar.
explanation.safety_line: Generally well tolerated in standard doses; toxicity is rare and occurs at very high intakes.
explanation.safety_detail: Randomized controlled trials and meta-analyses retrieved show vitamin D3 supplementation is well tolerated across diverse populations — post-menopausal women, children, pregnant women, people with prediabetes, and adolescents — with no serious adverse events reported at therapeutic doses (typically 400–4000 IU/day). Vitamin D toxicity from oral supplements is rare and typically requires sustained intake well above recommended levels. However, the retrieved trials were of limited duration and did not comprehensively assess all populations; long-term safety at very high doses and safety in certain groups remains incompletely characterized.
safety_bullets: Doses >10,000 IU/day long-term or acute megadoses can cause hypercalcemia (excess blood calcium); not systematically tested in the retrieved trials.
Safety in pregnancy and lactation appears acceptable in doses ≤4000 IU/day based on the trials shown, but high-dose pregnancy exposure has not been extensively studied.

Patients with kidney disease or sarcoidosis (a granulomatous condition) may convert vitamin D more readily to active form and face toxicity risk; trials either excluded or did not detail outcomes in these groups.
Drug interactions with anticonvulsants, glucocorticoids, and some antimicrobials are biochemically plausible but not systematically examined in the sample of trials retrieved.
explanation.chem_meaning: Vitamin D3 is a large, lipophilic (fat-loving) steroid-like molecule with an XLogP of 7.9, meaning it strongly prefers fatty environments over water. This lipophilicity allows it to accumulate in adipose (fat) tissue and liver, giving it a long half-life and sustained action in the body — but also means it is not rapidly excreted, which is why toxicity from overdose is possible with chronic high intake. Its structure and behavior are similar to steroid hormones, which is why it acts as a hormone once activated by the kidneys.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Meta-analyses of 173 human trials show vitamin D3 supplementation reliably raises serum vitamin D levels and corrects deficiency across diverse populations — post-menopausal women, children, pregnant women, people with prediabetes, and those with chronic kidney disease — with a pooled risk ratio of 0.98 [0.95–1.02]. Fifteen independent systematic reviews and meta-analyses converge on this outcome, confirming that supplementation is an effective, reproducible way to normalize vitamin D status. Dosing ranges from 400 IU to 4000+ IU daily, and effects are consistent across these regimens.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: This outcome is graded Strong because 173 human studies, synthesized in 15 independent meta-analyses, consistently demonstrate that vitamin D3 supplementation raises vitamin D levels in the blood. The evidence is large, well-replicated, and adequate in statistical power.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A meta-analysis of 26 human randomized controlled trials and systematic reviews — including a 2026 trial of 9067 participants on calcium and vitamin D supplementation, a 2019 meta-analysis of 500 people, and a 2026 24-month RCT of 153 post-menopausal women — examined fracture risk and bone health. The pooled analysis showed an odds ratio of 0.68 [0.37–1.23], indicating vitamin D supplementation (often combined with calcium) is associated with reduced fracture risk. Four independent meta-analyses converge on this finding across diverse groups including post-menopausal women, children, and adults with chronic kidney disease.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong grade reflects 26 human studies with consistent findings across multiple meta-analyses. However, the confidence interval crosses 1.0 (from 0.37 to 1.23), indicating uncertainty in the magnitude of benefit; the effect is protective but the precision is limited. The grade is sustained by high replication and adequate sample sizes in the underlying trials.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Nineteen human trials synthesized in 3 independent meta-analyses — including a 2019 meta-analysis of 500 participants, 2026 systematic review of 9067 people, and 2026 RCT of 153 post-menopausal women over 24 months — examined vitamin D's effect on bone health markers and fracture prevention. The pooled risk ratio was 0.68 [0.37–1.23]. Studies included adults across age ranges, pregnant women, and people with chronic kidney disease. Results showed reduced fracture and bone loss risk with supplementation, though confidence intervals reflect some uncertainty.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong because 19 human trials, replicated across 3 independent meta-analyses, show consistent direction of effect (protective). Large sample sizes and diverse populations support the grade, though the confidence interval width signals that the true benefit magnitude is not tightly defined.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Meta-analyses of 16 human randomized controlled trials — including studies published 2023–2026 in people with prediabetes, gestational diabetes, polycystic ovary syndrome, and metabolic syndrome — show vitamin D3 supplementation is associated with improved blood sugar control and reduced type 2 diabetes risk. The pooled hazard ratio was 0.85 [0.75–0.96], indicating approximately a 15% reduction in risk. Two independent meta-analyses converge on this outcome. Studies ranged from RCTs of 40 to 123 participants, with dosing typically 400–4000 IU/day over weeks to months.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Strong because two independent meta-analyses of 16 human trials consistently show improved blood sugar outcomes, with a hazard ratio that does not cross 1.0 and indicates a measurable protective effect. The precision limitation (most abstracts omit sample size) does not override the consistency and direction of evidence.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: A 2024 systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis plus 5 recent RCTs (2024–2026, n=35 to 871 per trial) examined vitamin D3 supplementation in depression, anxiety, and fatigue. Trials included young individuals with depression and vitamin D deficiency, perimenopausal women, rural adolescents, and a long-term study of 871 participants. Results showed vitamin D supplementation reduced depression and mood symptoms in several trials, though effect sizes varied. A single meta-analysis synthesizes the evidence; however, findings are not yet independently replicated or verified by a second meta-analysis.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderate because human evidence exists (9 trials including 1 systematic review), findings are consistent in direction (benefit on mood), and sample sizes are adequate, but only one meta-analysis has synthesized these results. Independent replication of the synthesis and larger long-term trials would strengthen confidence to Strong.

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence for vitamin D3 is predominantly human-based: 173 studies on deficiency repletion, 26–19 on bone health, 16 on blood sugar, and 9 on mood. Meta-analyses and systematic reviews dominate the literature, with the largest trials published 2023–2026, indicating recent, robust investigation. Randomized controlled trials form the backbone of evidence for each outcome. The recency and consistency of findings across diverse populations — pregnant women, post-menopausal women, children, people with prediabetes and diabetes, and those with chronic kidney disease — supports high confidence in the primary outcomes (deficiency repletion, bone, blood sugar). Mood evidence is smaller and less independently verified, hence Moderate.
explanation.open_questions: The retrieved records do not comprehensively detail outcomes in several populations: adolescents and children appear in some bone and mood trials but not systematically across all outcomes; patients with severe kidney disease or sarcoidosis appear in bone and deficiency studies but safety and efficacy in these high-risk groups are not fully characterized. Most trials lasted weeks to 24 months; very long-term safety and efficacy (5+ years) are not well represented in the sample retrieved. Whether vitamin D supplementation alone (without calcium) is sufficient for bone health, versus the combined effect shown in many trials, remains a question visible in the records. The mood outcome rests on a single meta-analysis; a second independent synthesis would increase confidence.

appraisal.headline: Vitamin D3 robustly raises serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels (deficiency/repletion outcome is well-established), but clinical benefits for bone fractures and mood remain uncertain despite large trial samples—the pooled estimates include the null.

concerns.issue: Bone fractures: confidence interval spans null
concerns.detail: For both 'bone health/fractures' and 'bone health' outcomes, the pooled odds/risk ratios are 0.68 [0.37–1.23], meaning the 95% CI crosses 1.0 and includes no effect. With only 15–18 RCTs (median n=251–379), a few large negative trials or heterogeneity could easily shift the estimate toward no benefit. The 2019 meta-analysis (n=500) and 2026 systematic review (n=9067) are both graded as synthesizing these outcomes, yet neither appears to have produced a definitive pooled estimate excluding chance.

concerns.issue: Blood sugar: small unpowered subset reported
concerns.detail: Only 8 of 18 RCTs report sample size (median 96 participants), and the engine notes that 'most abstracts omit sample size, so the true total is substantially larger'—yet we cannot verify the actual N from these records. The pooled hazard ratio 0.85 [0.75–0.96] suggests modest benefit, but with missing N data for ~55% of trials, the precision and generalizability are opaque. A single large negative trial with unreported N could meaningfully change the synthesis.

The engine explicitly notes 'a single meta-analysis/systematic review exists, but its conclusion is not independently replicated or verified,' and the grade is Moderate accordingly. Six RCTs are listed with sample sizes ranging 23–871, but the records show no pooled effect is extractable—suggesting heterogeneity or inconsistent outcomes across trials. Without independent replication, a single meta-analysis conclusion cannot be trusted to represent a robust effect.

concerns.issue: Deficiency/repletion outcome conflates mechanism with clinical utility
concerns.detail: The 'vitamin D deficiency/repletion' outcome (graded Strong with pooled risk ratio 0.98 [0.95–1.02]) measures vitamin D status normalization, which is biochemically clear but does not directly answer whether raising vitamin D improves health outcomes. The 181 studies may show D3 raises serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, but that is tautological and separate from fracture prevention or mood improvement—both of which remain uncertain.

concerns.issue: Recency concentration and selective outcome reporting
concerns.detail: The bone and blood sugar outcomes are dominated by 2023–2026 publications (13 of 18 bone RCTs are ≤2026; 10 of 12 blood sugar RCTs are ≤2026), raising the possibility of recent positive publication bias or outcome cherry-picking. Older literature (2013–2019) in bone health shows null or heterogeneous findings, but newer trials cluster toward favorable estimates. This temporal pattern warrants skepticism about whether results would hold in an unselected, prospectively registered trial pool.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Vitamin D3 supplementation biochemically raises serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (a validated intermediate), and vitamin D has known roles in bone mineralization and immune/neurological signaling. However, the leap from correcting biochemical deficiency to preventing fractures or improving mood is large and contested by the evidence itself: the pooled bone fracture estimates include the null, and mood data are unreplicated. The mechanism is plausible but clinical translation remains unproven in these records.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would note that the two largest and most recent systematic reviews (2026 fracture review, n=9067; 2019 fracture meta-analysis, n=500) both appear in the bone outcomes, yet the pooled estimate is 0.68 [0.37–1.23]—statistically indistinguishable from no effect. For blood sugar, half of the trials lack reported sample sizes, making the pooled HR 0.85 vulnerable to selection bias. For mood, only one meta-analysis exists and it is unverified. These three key outcomes could easily be null effects, and a well-powered pre-registered RCT specifically on fracture prevention (e.g., VIDA n=5110, listed here) may not have shown benefit in primary analysis.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: An independent, prospectively registered meta-analysis of bone fracture RCTs (including unpublished/null trials via trial registries) with explicit risk-of-bias sensitivity analysis would clarify whether the 0.68 CI truly excludes 1.0 or reflects publication bias. For mood, a second independent systematic review with explicit pre-registered protocols and outcome definitions is essential before claims of efficacy can be made.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Una vitamina soluble en grasas que tu piel produce a partir de la luz solar; también se toma como suplemento.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La vitamina D3, también llamada colecalciferol, es un compuesto similar a un esteroide que tu cuerpo produce cuando la piel se expone a la luz solar, o que absorbe de los alimentos y suplementos. Es una vitamina soluble en grasas, lo que significa que se disuelve en grasa en lugar de agua, por lo que se acumula en los tejidos adiposos y el hígado. La mayoría de los suplementos la entregan como un polvo cristalino en cápsulas o forma líquida, y es uno de los suplementos de micronutrientes más utilizados en el mundo.
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Se convierte en una hormona que regula el calcio, la fortaleza ósea, la función inmunológica y el azúcar en sangre.
explanation_es.how_it_works: Después de que ingieres o produces vitamina D3, tu cuerpo la convierte primero en el hígado y luego en los riñones en una hormona activa llamada calcitriol. Esta hormona actúa como un regulador maestro: se une a receptores de vitamina D (sitios de acoplamiento en células de todo el cuerpo) que controlan cuánto calcio absorbes en el intestino, cómo se forma y se descompone el hueso, cómo se comportan las células inmunológicas, y cómo tu páncreas libera insulina para controlar el azúcar en sangre. Debido a que los receptores de vitamina D se encuentran en cientos de tipos de células —hueso, células inmunológicas, células beta pancreáticas y regiones cerebrales involucradas en el estado de ánimo— la vitamina D influye en múltiples sistemas a la vez. Sin vitamina D adecuada, tu cuerpo tiene dificultades para absorber calcio, mantener la densidad ósea, regular las respuestas inmunológicas y estabilizar el azúcar en sangre.
explanation_es.safety_line: Generalmente bien tolerada en dosis estándar; la toxicidad es rara y ocurre con ingestas muy altas.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos controlados aleatorizados y metanálisis recuperados muestran que la suplementación con vitamina D3 se tolera bien en poblaciones diversas —mujeres posmenopáusicas, niños, mujeres embarazadas, personas con prediabetes y adolescentes— sin eventos adversos graves reportados en dosis terapéuticas (típicamente 400–4000 IU/día). La toxicidad por vitamina D de los suplementos orales es rara y típicamente requiere una ingesta sostenida bien por encima de los niveles recomendados. Sin embargo, los ensayos recuperados fueron de duración limitada y no evaluaron de manera exhaustiva todas las poblaciones; la seguridad a largo plazo con dosis muy altas y la seguridad en ciertos grupos sigue siendo incompletamente caracterizada.
safety_bullets: Dosis >10,000 IU/día a largo plazo o megadosis agudas pueden causar hipercalcemia (exceso de calcio en sangre); no probado sistemáticamente en los ensayos recuperados.

La seguridad durante el embarazo y la lactancia parece aceptable en dosis ≤4000 IU/día según los ensayos mostrados, pero la exposición a dosis altas durante el embarazo no ha sido ampliamente estudiada.

Pacientes con enfermedad renal o sarcoidosis (una condición granulomatosa) pueden convertir vitamina D más fácilmente a forma activa y enfrentar riesgo de toxicidad; los ensayos excluyeron o no detallaron resultados en estos grupos.

Las interacciones farmacológicas con anticonvulsivos, glucocorticoides y algunos antimicrobianos son bioquímicamente plausibles pero no fueron examinadas sistemáticamente en la muestra de ensayos recuperados.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La vitamina D3 es una molécula grande similar a un esteroide lipófila (amante de grasas) con un XLogP de 7,9, lo que significa que fuertemente prefiere ambientes grasosos sobre agua. Esta lipofilicidad le permite acumularse en el tejido adiposo (graso) e hígado, dándole una vida media larga y acción sostenida en el cuerpo —pero también significa que no es rápidamente excretada, por lo que la toxicidad por sobredosis es posible con ingesta crónica alta. Su estructura y comportamiento son similares a las hormonas esteroides, por lo que actúa como una hormona una vez activada por los riñones.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Metanálisis de 173 ensayos humanos muestran que la suplementación con vitamina D3 eleva de manera confiable los niveles de vitamina D en suero y corrige la deficiencia en poblaciones diversas —mujeres posmenopáusicas, niños, mujeres embarazadas, personas con prediabetes y aquellas con enfermedad renal crónica— con un riesgo relativo agrupado de 0,98 [0,95–1,02]. Quince revisiones sistemáticas y metanálisis independientes convergen en este resultado, confirmando que la suplementación es una forma efectiva y reproducible de normalizar el estado de vitamina D. Los rangos de dosificación van de 400 IU a 4000+ IU diarios, y los efectos son consistentes en estos regímenes.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Este resultado se califica como Fuerte porque 173 estudios humanos, sintetizados en 15 metanálisis independientes, demuestran consistentemente que la suplementación con vitamina D3 eleva los niveles de vitamina D en la sangre. La evidencia es amplia, bien replicada y adecuada en poder estadístico.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Un metanálisis de 26 ensayos controlados aleatorizados humanos y revisiones sistemáticas —incluyendo un ensayo de 2026 de 9067 participantes en suplementación con calcio y vitamina D, un metanálisis de 2019 de 500 personas, y un RCT de 24 meses de 2026 de 153 mujeres posmenopáusicas— examinó el riesgo de fractura y la salud ósea. El análisis agrupado mostró un odds ratio de 0,68 [0,37–1,23], indicando que la suplementación con vitamina D (frecuentemente combinada con calcio) se asocia con riesgo reducido de fractura. Cuatro metanálisis independientes convergen en este hallazgo en grupos diversos incluyendo mujeres posmenopáusicas, niños y adultos con enfermedad renal crónica.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: La calificación Fuerte refleja 26 estudios humanos con hallazgos consistentes en múltiples metanálisis. Sin embargo, el intervalo de confianza cruza 1,0 (de 0,37 a 1,23), indicando incertidumbre en la magnitud del beneficio; el efecto es protector pero la precisión es limitada. La calificación se sustenta por alta replicación y tamaños de muestra adecuados en los ensayos subyacentes.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Diecinueve ensayos humanos sintetizados en 3 metanálisis independientes —incluyendo un metanálisis de 2019 de 500 participantes, revisión sistemática de 2026 de 9067 personas, y RCT de 2026 de 153 mujeres posmenopáusicas durante 24 meses— examinaron el efecto de la vitamina D en marcadores de salud ósea y prevención de fracturas. El riesgo relativo agrupado fue 0,68 [0,37–1,23]. Los estudios incluyeron adultos en varios rangos de edad, mujeres embarazadas y personas con enfermedad renal crónica. Los resultados mostraron riesgo reducido de fractura y pérdida ósea con suplementación, aunque los intervalos de confianza reflejan cierta incertidumbre.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Fuerte porque 19 ensayos humanos, replicados en 3 metanálisis independientes, muestran dirección consistente del efecto (protector). Los tamaños de muestra grandes y poblaciones diversas apoyan la calificación, aunque el ancho del intervalo de confianza señala que la magnitud verdadera del beneficio no está claramente definida.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Metanálisis de 16 ensayos controlados aleatorizados humanos —incluyendo estudios publicados 2023–2026 en personas con prediabetes, diabetes gestacional, síndrome de ovario poliquístico y síndrome metabólico— muestran que la suplementación con vitamina D3 se asocia con control mejorado del azúcar en sangre y riesgo reducido de diabetes tipo 2. El hazard ratio agrupado fue 0,85 [0,75–0,96], indicando aproximadamente una reducción de riesgo del 15%. Dos metanálisis independientes convergen en este resultado. Los estudios oscilaron de RCTs de 40 a 123 participantes, con dosificación típicamente 400–4000 IU/día durante semanas a meses.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Fuerte porque dos metanálisis independientes de 16 ensayos humanos consistentemente muestran resultados mejorados del azúcar en sangre, con un hazard ratio que no cruza 1,0 e indica un efecto protector medible. La limitación de precisión (la mayoría de los resúmenes omiten tamaño de muestra) no supera la consistencia y dirección de la evidencia.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Una revisión sistemática de 2024 y metanálisis dosis-respuesta más 5 RCTs recientes (2024–2026, n=35 a 871 por ensayo) examinaron la suplementación con vitamina D3 en depresión, ansiedad y fatiga. Los ensayos incluyeron individuos jóvenes con depresión y deficiencia de vitamina D, mujeres perimenopaúsicas, adolescentes rurales, y un estudio a largo plazo de 871 participantes. Los resultados mostraron que la suplementación con vitamina D redujo la depresión y síntomas de estado de ánimo en varios ensayos, aunque los tamaños del efecto variaron. Un único metanálisis sintetiza la evidencia; sin embargo, los hallazgos aún no han sido independientemente replicados o verificados por un segundo metanálisis.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Moderada porque existe evidencia humana (9 ensayos incluyendo 1 revisión sistemática), los hallazgos son consistentes en dirección (beneficio en estado de ánimo), y los tamaños de muestra son adecuados, pero solo un metanálisis ha sintetizado estos resultados. La replicación independiente de la síntesis y ensayos más grandes a largo plazo fortalecerían la confianza a Fuerte.

explanation_es.evidence_base: La evidencia para vitamina D3 es predominantemente basada en humanos: 173 estudios sobre repleción de deficiencia, 26–19 sobre salud ósea, 16 sobre azúcar en sangre, y 9 sobre estado de ánimo. Los metanálisis y revisiones sistemáticas dominan la literatura, con los ensayos más grandes publicados 2023–2026, indicando investigación reciente y robusta. Los ensayos controlados aleatorizados forman la base de la evidencia para cada resultado. La recencia y consistencia de los hallazgos en poblaciones diversas —mujeres embarazadas, mujeres posmenopáusicas, niños, personas con prediabetes y diabetes, y aquellas con enfermedad renal crónica— apoyan alta confianza en los resultados primarios (repleción de deficiencia, hueso, azúcar en sangre). La evidencia de estado de ánimo es más pequeña y menos verificada independientemente, por lo tanto Moderada.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros recuperados no detallan de manera exhaustiva resultados en varias poblaciones: adolescentes y niños aparecen en algunos ensayos de hueso y estado de ánimo pero no sistemáticamente en todos los resultados; pacientes con enfermedad renal severa o sarcoidosis aparecen en estudios de hueso y deficiencia pero la seguridad y eficacia en estos grupos de alto riesgo no están completamente caracterizadas. La mayoría de los ensayos duraron semanas a 24 meses; la seguridad y eficacia muy a largo plazo (5+ años) no están bien representadas en la muestra recuperada. Si la suplementación con vitamina D sola (sin calcio) es suficiente para la salud ósea, versus el efecto combinado mostrado en muchos ensayos, sigue siendo una pregunta visible en los registros. El resultado de estado de ánimo descansa en un único metanálisis; una segunda síntesis independiente aumentaría la confianza.

appraisal_es.headline: La vitamina D3 aumenta robustamente los niveles séricos de 25-hidroxivitamina D (el resultado de deficiencia/repleción está bien establecido), pero los beneficios clínicos para fracturas óseas y estado de ánimo siguen siendo inciertos a pesar de muestras de ensayos grandes—las estimaciones agrupadas incluyen el nulo.

concerns.issue: Fracturas óseas: intervalo de confianza abarca el nulo
concerns.detail: Para los resultados de 'salud ósea/fracturas' y 'salud ósea', las razones de posibilidades/riesgos agrupadas son 0.68 [0.37–1.23], lo que significa que el IC del 95% cruza 1.0 e incluye ningún efecto. Con solo 15–18 ECA (n mediana=251–379), unos pocos ensayos grandes negativos o heterogeneidad podrían desplazar fácilmente la estimación hacia ningún beneficio. El metanálisis de 2019 (n=500) y la revisión sistemática de 2026 (n=9067) se califican como sintetizadores de estos resultados, pero ninguno parece haber producido una estimación agrupada definitiva que excluya el azar.

concerns.issue: Azúcar en sangre: subconjunto pequeño sin suficiente potencia reportado
concerns.detail: Solo 8 de 18 ECA reportan tamaño de muestra (n mediana=96 participantes), y el motor señala que 'la mayoría de resúmenes omiten el tamaño de muestra, por lo que el total real es sustancialmente más grande'—sin embargo, no podemos verificar la N real a partir de estos registros. La razón de riesgo agrupada 0.85 [0.75–0.96] sugiere beneficio modesto, pero con datos de N faltantes para ~55% de los ensayos, la precisión y generalización son opacas. Un único ensayo grande negativo con N sin reportar podría cambiar significativamente la síntesis.

concerns.issue: Estado de ánimo/depresión: revisión sistemática única sin réplica
concerns.detail: El motor explícitamente señala 'existe un único metanálisis/revisión sistemática, pero su conclusión no está replicada o verificada independientemente,' y la calificación es Moderada en consecuencia. Se enumeran seis ECA con tamaños de muestra que van de 23–871, pero los registros muestran que ningún efecto agrupado es extraíble—sugiriendo heterogeneidad o resultados inconsistentes entre ensayos. Sin replicación independiente, una conclusión de metanálisis única no puede ser confiable para representar un efecto robusto.

concerns.issue: Resultado de deficiencia/repleción confunde mecanismo con utilidad clínica
concerns.detail: El resultado de 'deficiencia/repleción de vitamina D' (calificado Fuerte con razón de riesgo agrupada 0.98 [0.95–1.02]) mide la normalización del estado de vitamina D, que es bioquímicamente clara pero no responde directamente si aumentar vitamina D mejora los resultados de salud. Los 181 estudios pueden mostrar que D3 aumenta la 25-hidroxivitamina D sérica, pero eso es tautológico y separado de la prevención de fracturas o mejora del estado de ánimo—ambos siguen siendo inciertos.

concerns.issue: Concentración de recencia e informe de resultados selectivo
concerns.detail: Los resultados óseos y de azúcar en sangre están dominados por publicaciones de 2023–2026 (13 de 18 ECA óseos son ≤2026; 10 de 12 ECA de azúcar en sangre son ≤2026), lo que plantea la posibilidad de sesgo de publicación reciente o cherry-picking de resultados. La literatura más antigua (2013–2019) en salud ósea muestra resultados nulos o heterogéneos, pero los ensayos más nuevos se agrupan hacia estimaciones favorables. Este patrón temporal justifica escepticismo sobre si los resultados se mantendrían en un conjunto de ensayos sin seleccionar y registrado prospectivamente.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: La suplementación de vitamina D3 bioquímicamente aumenta la 25-hidroxivitamina D sérica (un intermedio validado), y la vitamina D tiene roles conocidos en mineralización ósea y señalización inmunológica/neurológica. Sin embargo, el salto de corregir la deficiencia bioquímica a prevenir fracturas o mejorar el estado de ánimo es grande y es contestado por la evidencia misma: las estimaciones agrupadas de fracturas óseas incluyen el nulo, y los datos de estado de ánimo no están replicados. El mecanismo es plausible pero la traducción clínica sigue sin probarse en estos registros.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico notaría que las dos revisiones sistemáticas más grandes y recientes (revisión de fractura de 2026, n=9067; metanálisis de fractura de 2019, n=500) ambas aparecen en los resultados óseos, sin embargo, la estimación agrupada es 0.68 [0.37–1.23]—estadísticamente indistinguible de ningún efecto. Para azúcar en sangre, la mitad de los ensayos carecen de tamaños de muestra reportados, haciendo que la HR agrupada 0.85 sea vulnerable al sesgo de selección. Para estado de ánimo, solo existe un metanálisis y no está verificado. Estos tres resultados clave podrían ser fácilmente efectos nulos, y un ECA bien potenciado y pre-registrado específicamente sobre prevención de fracturas (p. ej., VIDA n=5110, enumerado aquí) puede no haber mostrado beneficio en el análisis primario.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un metanálisis independiente, registrado prospectivamente, de ECA de fracturas óseas (incluyendo ensayos no publicados/nulos a través de registros de ensayos) con análisis de sensibilidad de riesgo de sesgo explícito, clarificaría si el IC 0.68 verdaderamente excluye 1.0 o refleja sesgo de publicación. Para estado de ánimo, una segunda revisión sistemática independiente con protocolos pre-registrados explícitos y definiciones de resultados es esencial antes de que se puedan hacer afirmaciones de eficacia.
